land.text: all of Libya, the same outline

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's row boundary, not a break in the state: the Libya page treats Libya as one country under successive names (Kingdom 1951, Libyan Arab Republic after the 1969 coup, Jamahiriya from 2 March 1977, 'officially the State of Libya', a name the UN was told in December 2017 was 'henceforth' official). The Libyan Arab Republic dossier ends in 2013 and hands over to this one.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: 'The capital and largest city is Tripoli.' The elected House of Representatives met at Tobruk from 2014 ('forcing the newly elected parliament to flee to Tobruk'), and 'Both governments have been functioning simultaneously' since March 2022.

keyframe_review.note: 1,614,019 km2 against the infobox 1,759,541 km2 (ratio 0.92, fine); the outline is the Libyan Arab Republic's, unchanged. The page records no change of Libya's international borders after 2014, only a claim to '32,000 square kilometres of southeastern Algeria, south of the Libyan town of Ghat'. The de facto division between the House of Representatives (Tobruk) and the Government of National Unity (Tripoli) is not drawn: no page opened dates a front line.
Identical to the 2014 shape; the page says control is 'split between the House of Representatives (HoR) in Tobruk' and the GNU in Tripoli 'plus militias and tribal groups' but gives no boundary.

region.text: all of Libya, the same outline as the Libyan Arab Republic

ledger.note: 2014: Cliopatria's State of Libya begins as Libya splits between rival parliaments. The Second Libyan Civil War page: 'At the beginning of 2014, Libya was governed by the General National Congress' which 'failed to stand down at the end of its electoral mandate in January 2014'; the Libya page: 'In June 2014, elections were held to the House of Representatives' and 'The Second Civil War began in May 2014 following fighting between rival parliaments.' Neither page marks a new state: the start year is Cliopatria's row boundary (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 2019: Haftar's army advances on Tripoli. 'On 4 April 2019, Khalifa Haftar, the commander of the Libyan National Army, ... called on his military forces to advance on Tripoli' in 'the 2019-20 Western Libya campaign'; the LNA was allied in Tarhuna with the al-Kaniyat militia (Libyan National Army page). The page does not date any gain of ground.

ledger.note: 2020: a permanent ceasefire ends the war. 'On 23 October 2020, the 5+5 Joint Libyan Military Commission representing the LNA and the GNA reached a permanent ceasefire agreement in all areas of Libya'; before it, 'In 2020, the GNA forces successfully ousted the militia and the UAE-backed Haftar's forces and captured Tarhuna' (month not given). The war 'concluded on 24 October 2020'; an interim unity government was formed on 10 March 2021.

wars.outcome: A permanent ceasefire on 23 October 2020 between the LNA and the GNA, then an interim unity government (10 March 2021); the page says that since March 2022, when the House of Representatives 'ceased recognising' the Government of National Unity, 'Both governments have been functioning simultaneously'.
wars.note: Dated steps on the page: Operation Dignity 16 May 2014 (Haftar); Libya Dawn captured Tripoli airport from the Zintan militia on 23 August 2014 and the House of Representatives moved to Tobruk; 6 November 2014 the Tripoli supreme court declared it dissolved; ISIL expelled from Derna in July 2015; 17 December 2015 agreement on a unity government; May 2016 GNA and GNC offensive on Sirte against ISIL; Benghazi retaken from ISIL in 2017; Derna 2018. Territorial control by region is not given, so only the 2019-2020 Tripoli front is drawn as a zone.

certainty.note: Libya's international frontiers are not discussed on the pages opened beyond a claim on southeastern Algeria south of Ghat, which stays soft; the internal division between Tobruk and Tripoli has no line on any page and is not drawn.

notes: Page budget 1-2: three pages opened (Libya, Second Libyan Civil War, Libyan National Army); the third gave no territorial dates. (1) Cliopatria's State of Libya begins in 2014; the Libya page treats it as the same country as the Libyan Arab Republic (and the Kingdom of Libya): three dossiers exist for one country under successive regimes (kingdom-of-libya, libyan-arab-republic, state-of-libya). data/README.md lists 'Kingdom of Libya / State of Libya' among the Names that share a Wikidata id, but polities.csv gives them Q31454 and Q1016, so they are different rows for different regimes, not one row twice. The colour agent may keep one hue; the start year 2014 follows the Libyan Arab Republic dossier, which dissolves in 2013. (2) The de facto division from 2014 (the House of Representatives and the Libyan National Army in the east, the General National Congress and later the GNA/GNU in Tripoli) is not drawn: no page opened gives a front line, a dated capture or the area each side held; the LNA page names only 'Eastern, central and southern Libya' as active regions. A gap-filler should open the battle pages that the LNA page lists: Battle of Benghazi (2014-2017), Siege of Derna, Battle of Sabha (2019), Battle of Sirte (2020), Central Libya offensive 2020, and the oil crescent and Fezzan pages, and add an LNA rebel/rival dossier. Counterparts 'libyan-national-army', 'General National Congress' and 'Government of National Accord' need dossiers (slugs libyan-national-army, general-national-congress, government-of-national-accord). (3) The month of the 2019 contest_start is the page's 4 April call to advance; the page does not say when ground was taken. (4) Gazetteer: 'Tarhuna' is unknown (Libya, about 65 km south-east of Tripoli). (5) No rulers are listed: the page names a Presidential Council head (Mohamed al-Menfi) and prime ministers without term dates. (6) Not recorded for lack of a page: the Aouzou Strip (settled 1994, in the Libyan Arab Republic dossier), the claim on southeastern Algeria (a claim, not an event).
